reason: I'd probably run the free 14 days since there's no auto-charge and the daytime-sleep part actually fits my mornings after nights, but I wouldn't pay off the back of numbers measured by a phone lying on the mattress. I already fall asleep to free sounds on YouTube, so the app has to prove itself to me first.
objection: Can a phone by the bed really tell when I fell asleep? If I put it down and lie there scrolling thoughts for 40 minutes, or my partner moves, the 'time to fall asleep' comparison could just be noise, and then the whole 14-day report means nothing.
would_change_my_mind: If my own 14-day comparison showed a clear gap, and it matched what a watch recorded on the same days (or there were solid app-store reviews from other shift workers saying the same), I'd pay the yearly 39,000.
